knowledge:
- key_parameters: select=Specifies a subset of samples to visualize, accepting a numeric vector of indices or a character vector of sample names ;; probes=Specifies probe types to include for PM/MM platforms (e.g., "mm" or "all"; default is PM only) ;; empty.rows=Controls how empty rows are handled ("fill" to interpolate from neighbors, "ignore" to leave empty) ;; empty.thresh=Numeric threshold (default 0.60) defining the proportion of missing values above which a row is considered empty and filled ;; nrow=Manually specifies the number of rows in the multi-array plotting grid ;; ncol=Manually specifies the number of columns in the multi-array plotting grid ;; type=For PLM objects, refers to the model value type (e.g., residuals or weights) rather than probe type ;; transform=A function (e.g., log2, arank, arle) that transforms the 3D array of intensities prior to visualization ;; colors=A vector of colors to use for the image palette ;; legend.label=Character string to customize the legend title
- alternatives: affy::image() or oligo::image()=Standard plotting methods for specific microarray classes, but mimager::mimage() is preferred for its consistent interface across multiple classes, automatic legend generation, row-filling to prevent rasterization artifacts, and multi-array grid layouts ;; affyPLM::fitPLM() and oligo::fitProbeLevelModel()=Used to fit the probe-level models themselves, which mimager then visualizes
- when_to_use: Use during the quality control (QC) phase of microarray data analysis to identify physical/spatial defects on the chips (e.g., bubbles, scratches, hybridization gradients) before downstream normalization and differential expression analysis
- pitfalls: Excluding probe types (like MM probes) can cause abundant missing values and rasterization artifacts; use empty.rows = "fill" (default) to mitigate this ;; Using base R rank() as a transform function will fail because it returns a numeric vector instead of preserving the 3D array structure; use mimager::arank() instead ;; When visualizing PLM objects, the type argument changes its meaning from probe type to model value type (residuals or weights)

workflows.name: raw_microarray_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize raw probe-level intensities across one or more microarray chips to inspect for spatial artifacts.
input: raw_microarray_data.RData (An AffyBatch, ExpressionFeatureSet, ExonFeatureSet, GeneFeatureSet, or SnpFeatureSet object containing raw microarray intensities)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the microarray data; 2. Visualize a single array or multiple arrays in a grid layout; 3. Customize probe selection and row-filling options.
workflows.code:
library(mimager)
library(affydata)
data("Dilution")
mimage(Dilution, select = 1)
mimage(Dilution)
mimage(Dilution, select = c("10A", "20A", "10B", "20B"), nrow = 1)

workflows.name: plm_spatial_artifact_visualization
workflows.intent: Fit a probe-level linear model (PLM) and visualize its residuals or weights to reveal subtle spatial artifacts.
input: raw_microarray_data.RData (An AffyBatch or oligo-compatible FeatureSet object containing raw microarray intensities)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit a probe-level linear model using affyPLM or oligo; 2. Plot the PLM residuals or weights using mimage.

workflows.name: transformed_array_visualization
workflows.intent: Convert microarray data to a 3D array and apply custom transformations (like RLE or rank) to highlight spatial biases.
input: raw_microarray_data.RData (An AffyBatch or FeatureSet object containing raw microarray intensities)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert microarray object to a 3D array; 2. Apply rank transformation or relative log expression (RLE) transformation; 3. Plot the transformed array with custom color palettes.
workflows.code:
div.colors <- scales::brewer_pal(palette = "RdBu")(9)
mimage(Dilution, transform = arle, legend.label = "RLE", colors = div.colors)
DilutionArray <- marray(Dilution)
dim(DilutionArray)
DilutionRank <- arank(DilutionArray)
dim(DilutionRank)
